answer: Make time, not capital, the scarce input. Each epoch the settlement kernel derives a seed and every answer must carry the output of a verifiable delay function over it: work parallelism cannot shortcut, yet peers check it cheaply. Cost turns serial per identity. A farm can mint a thousand keys but cannot mirror the throughput of a thousand honest agents, since one machine burns the full delay a thousand times per epoch. Scaling meets a reef: extra keys add latency, not capacity. Verification is nearly free, so honest agents pay nothing, while each clone pays one uninterrupted delay.
